svg.title: RB2.1.1 04c v6 — Component ID: merged chart, proportional split, info modal
svg.text: BEFORE — as built, on the headset now
priority = mass x EF 3.1 ADP (log) · recovery = arrival x yield
AFTER — 1 material, drawing takes the space
This material's share of the component's minerals and
metals footprint (EF 3.1 ADP). LOG scale — gold is 0.04 %
of the connector mass and 98 % of its impact.
— means the material has no EF 3.1 factor.
The share that survives the Scenario 4 route once the
material arrives in the right stream. LINEAR 0–100 %.
Source: Bigum et al. 2012, Table 8. 0 % = credited in
no scenario, which is an answer, not a gap.
1. The caption is gone in every state. "1 of 8 . 108.5 g" duplicated the list the user just came from and the mass already
in the row below it. The pill is now the only header text, and it never changes (00 §4.3).
2. PROPORTIONAL SPLIT. drawing = 284 - 10 - (14 + n x 20 + 18), clamped to [120, 232]. It closes exactly on the band:
n=1 -> drawing 222 (was 140, +59 %) n=3 -> 182 n=6 -> 122. No empty band under a 1-material part, no clipping at 6.
3. ONE CHART COLUMN, two 6-high bars sharing an origin: RECOVERY IMPACT above (green/gold), MAX RECOVERY RATE below
(blue). The two % columns on the right take the SAME colours, so the legend is the colour, not a key.
4. The "i" replaces the footnote. A 16-unit visual inside a 50-unit hit root (00 s4.2), instead of a 372-wide
sentence nobody reads twice. The modal is UI on the same canvas, so 00 s4.2 modal-depth does not apply here.
THE ONE THING I WOULD PUSH BACK ON — the merged column is honest only if the axes stay visibly different.
The impact bar is LOG (1e-6 % .. 100 %), the recovery bar is LINEAR (0..100 %). Same origin, same track width, same row:
they WILL be read as comparable lengths unless something says otherwise. Two things do the work here, and both must survive
into the build: the decade TICKS drawn behind the upper bar only, and the modal. Drop either and the chart lies quietly.
If the ticks read as noise on device, the fallback is to shorten the impact track to 3/4 width so the two never end level.
WHAT THE DATA SAYS THAT THE CHART CANNOT FIX
On 5 of the 8 parts ONE material carries 100.0 % of the impact - the housings (aluminium alone), and the three IC groups
(copper alone, everything else has no EF 3.1 factor). A full-width 100 % bar there is trivially true and reads as a finding.
The chart earns its keep on the CONNECTOR (gold 98.5 % of impact at 0.04 % of mass) and on ic_1 (tin 80.9 %). That is the
argument of the thesis, and it is visible on 2 of 8 screens. Worth deciding whether the other 6 should say so in words.
PAYLOAD BUG FOUND WHILE DRAWING THIS - impact_share_pct is stored rounded to 4 dp.
Connector aluminium HAS an EF 3.1 factor and a real 3e-6 % share, but stores as 0.0 - identical to polymers, which have NO
factor at all. The shipped build renders both as "-". They are different answers: "negligible" vs "not characterised".
This mock recomputes the share from impact_kg_sb_eq instead. Fix in the payload (more sig figs) before coding the panel.
